title: How this draft was checked
body: drafter wrote the page from the blueprint you approved in batch 3. A fresh fact-checker read 89 claims against the code: 76 held, 3 were wrong, 6 were imprecise, and 4 were unsupported. The register editor's 28 findings, 3 of them blocking, were applied. Two rechecks followed, 65 of 81 and then 72 of 75 holding, and each finding is fixed.

Four platform claims, Cloudflare's per-plan body limit and the Fetch standard's forbidden `Content-Length` header, now link the vendor page that states them. Each claim change was carried back to the blueprint.

anchor.quote: the response's HTTP status is the status the action passed to `fail()`

title: A refused upload answers with its own HTTP status
body: The draft said a refusal arrives inside a 200 envelope. That is SvelteKit 2 behavior. In SvelteKit 3.0.1 the response status is the `fail()` status, and the body is still the envelope (`actions.js:56-64`). The engine's clients read the body whatever the status (`MediaReplaceDialog.svelte:208-214`), so uploads work. The prose was stale in five places, and this PR fixes all five: this page, its blueprint, `f:g4cwcw`, `docs/reference/sveltekit.md`, and the upload action's TSDoc.

anchor.quote: doesn't resolve to an image URL

title: A missing resolver costs the hero image
body: The draft, a fact, and four other places said an unresolved `media:` reference renders as a literal token. With no `resolveMedia`, `createPublicRoutes` derives no hero image (`public-routes.ts:98`). Body images lose their source only when the site's `render` has no resolver of its own, and the scaffold's `render` falls back to `publicMediaResolver`. This PR corrects `f:twqb0s`, Debug your site, the `log-events` and `delivery` reference rows, and the `createPublicRoutes` TSDoc to say so.

anchor.quote: HTTP 413 response whose body isn't a JSON action envelope

title: Telling Cloudflare's 413 from the engine's
body: The action's own `too_large` refusal also answers 413, so the row now tells them apart by the body: Cloudflare's isn't a JSON action envelope. The draft's claims about when Cloudflare sends it, before the Worker runs and with no log record, came out. Cloudflare's pages state the 413 and not its timing.

anchor.quote: a width of at least 800 pixels

title: The responsive-image threshold is restored
body: The blueprint gave the 800-pixel floor, which the draft had smoothed into "wide enough". The width ladder is 400, 800, 1200, and 1600, and a `srcset` needs two rungs. `f:wdmlys` now also says a too-narrow asset keeps its intrinsic width and height.
